clue.text: Drink first of sherries, something going to one's head

indicators.note: first of asks for only the opening letter of the word that follows

parts.note: opening letter of sherries
a wig is worn on the head

explanation.surface: A sherry-drinker warns that the first glass goes straight to the head.
explanation.definitionFit: A swig is a large gulp taken from a drink, and swig is also the verb for gulping it.

clue.text: Underwear stocks, say?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: loose knickers once worn by women
second meaning: things that bloom, stocks being garden flowers

explanation.surface: A shop takes stock of its knicker supplies.
explanation.walkthrough: Stocks looks like a verb about keeping goods, but it is the scented garden flower, and any flower is something that blooms.
explanation.definitionFit: Bloomers are baggy knee-length knickers, and flowers such as stocks are literally plants that bloom.

clue.text: Dogs, say, misleading guards

indicators.note: the outer word guards, or holds inside it, a run of letters that forms the solution

parts.note: letters two to five of misleading

explanation.surface: Guard dogs that put intruders off the scent.
explanation.walkthrough: The Isle of Dogs is a district of East London in a loop of the Thames, so Dogs is one example of an isle.
explanation.definitionFit: The Isle of Dogs is an example of a place named as an isle, signalled by say.

clue.text: Shrew lifting bottom, tricky when tail removed earlier

indicators.note: earlier tells us the shortened word sits in front of the other piece
with its tail removed a word loses its last letter

parts.note: a tricky problem is a hard one

indicators.note: in a down entry, lifting means reading a word from bottom to top

parts.note: the nadir is the lowest point

explanation.surface: A cryptic account of a sly shrew sitting up and tucking its tail away.
explanation.walkthrough: Shrew looks like the small animal, but it is the old word for a nagging woman; bottom means the lowest point, not a backside.
explanation.definitionFit: A shrew in the old sense is a bad-tempered scolding woman, and harridan is a synonym.

clue.text: Tiddly brief

definitions.meaning: second meaning: condensed, as in a short summary of a history

explanation.surface: Someone only a little tipsy, and only briefly.
explanation.walkthrough: Tiddly is British slang for slightly drunk; potted is also slang for drunk.
explanation.definitionFit: Potted means drunk in slang, and a potted history is an abridged, shortened account.

clue.text: Politician: his being slightly inadequate, hole up when in jeopardy

indicators.note: when in places the preceding pieces inside the word that follows

parts.note: danger

indicators.note: slightly inadequate means falling just short, so one letter is lost from the end

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: in a down entry, up means the word is read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: a vulgar sense of hole

explanation.surface: A dig at a politician holed up and found wanting when his position is under threat.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is political satire, but the man it mocks is the answer itself; hole is used in its rude anatomical sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Rishi Sunak is a British Conservative politician who was Prime Minister from 2022 to 2024.

clue.text: Fourth, twenty-fourth and twenty-fifth letters, all going to the third, reportedly?

definitions.text: Fourth, twenty-fourth and twenty-fifth letters, all going to the third, reportedly?

parts.note: surface reading: the letters D, X and Y of the alphabet

parts.words: all going to the third, reportedly
parts.note: setter's reading: said aloud the letters sound like Dee, Exe and Wye, and the third letter sounds like sea, where they all flow

explanation.surface: An alphabet puzzle about letters heading towards C.
explanation.walkthrough: Spoken, D, X and Y are the Dee, Exe and Wye, British watercourses, and C sounds like sea, where they end up.
explanation.definitionFit: The Dee, Exe and Wye are all examples of British waterways that flow into the sea.

clue.text: Name associated with Facebook article, police onto that

indicators.note: in a down entry, onto puts one piece on top of the other

parts.note: the Met is London's Metropolitan Police
the indefinite article

explanation.surface: Police take an interest in a Facebook article.
explanation.definitionFit: Meta is the company name adopted in 2021 by the owner of Facebook.

clue.text: Author, I applaud your observation when 5?

indicators.note: 5 down is POTTED, meaning brief, so the phrase is cut short

parts.note: what you say to praise a remark

explanation.surface: Praise for a writer's remark made while a little drunk.
explanation.walkthrough: The cross-reference reads as tipsy but is used as brief: the phrase is shortened to its first five letters.
explanation.definitionFit: H. G. Wells was an English writer of science fiction such as The War of the Worlds.

clue.text: Go abroad with Iberian native

indicators.note: abroad suggests being scattered widely, so the letters are spread into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Travel advice: head overseas alongside a local from Spain.
explanation.definitionFit: An aborigine is an original inhabitant of a land, i.e. a native of it.

clue.text: Travel Lodge's opening in sweet marsh to the west

indicators.note: in an across entry, going west means reading right to left

parts.note: a rich layered cake

indicators.note: in places the first letter inside the next word

parts.note: wet ground

indicators.note: a word's opening is its first letter

parts.note: first letter of Lodge

explanation.surface: A hotel chain advertisement with a dessert and some soggy ground thrown in.
explanation.walkthrough: Travelodge is a British budget hotel chain; the setter splits its name so Travel becomes the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To globetrot is to travel widely around the world, so it is a verb synonym.

clue.text: Animal they see, Noah seeing every second

indicators.note: every second asks for letters two, four, six and so on

parts.note: the even-placed letters of these words

explanation.surface: The animals Noah watches boarding the ark, two by two.
explanation.definitionFit: The hyena is a dog-like scavenging carnivore of Africa and Asia, an example of an animal.

clue.text: See 19
Nice one: shocker verboten

parts.note: ta is British slang for thanks, which nice one also expresses
a boo is shouted to give someone a fright

explanation.surface: A French city, a German word and a scandal: nice reads like the Riviera town.
explanation.walkthrough: Nice looks like the French city or an adjective; it goes with one as a thank-you.
explanation.definitionFit: Verboten is German for forbidden, and a taboo thing is socially prohibited.

clue.text: Similar doctor arrested by dodgy Irish cop

indicators.note: someone arrested by others is held inside them
something dodgy is not straight, so these letters need rearranging

parts.note: taken as written
MO is a medical officer

explanation.surface: A bent policeman in Ireland collars a doctor.
explanation.definitionFit: Isomorphic means having the same form or structure, so it is a technical word for alike.

clue.text: Work out when filling gone — empty?

indicators.note: a filling goes inside, so the first piece sits within the second

parts.note: passed away
to sus out, or suss, is to work something out

explanation.surface: A dentist's verdict that a tooth emptied of its filling is beyond repair.
explanation.walkthrough: Sus out is a spelling variant of suss out. The question mark admits that a disused building is only usually empty.
explanation.definitionFit: A disused building is no longer in use, so it typically stands vacant, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Minute completed and day ends

parts.note: did a job means completed it

indicators.note: the ends of a word are its first and last letters

parts.note: first and last letters of day

explanation.surface: A tiny task finished, and the working day is over.
explanation.walkthrough: Minute here is the adjective (my-NEWT), not sixty seconds. Diddy is British informal for small.
explanation.definitionFit: Diddy is informal British for tiny, a colloquial synonym of the adjective minute.

clue.text: Club's last, equally true voice

indicators.note: last means only the final letter of that word is kept

parts.note: final letter of club
as in as good, meaning equally good
is that so? means is that true?

explanation.surface: A golf or card club's final word, fair and accurate.
explanation.definitionFit: A basso is a bass singer, the lowest male voice in a choir or opera.

clue.text: Horse and badger

definitions.meaning: first meaning: an old or poor horse
second meaning: as a verb, to pester

explanation.surface: Two animals side by side in a field.
explanation.walkthrough: Badger looks like an animal but is the verb meaning pester.
explanation.definitionFit: A nag is a worn-out horse, and to nag someone is to pester them repeatedly.

clue.text: Like Dorothy's house in 1939 film?

parts.note: surface reading: the house in The Wizard of Oz, itself a 1939 film
setter's reading: the house was carried off by a tornado, which describes the title of a different 1939 film

explanation.surface: A question about the Kansas farmhouse in The Wizard of Oz.
explanation.walkthrough: The 1939 film looks like The Wizard of Oz, but the answer is the other big film that year, whose title describes the tornado-borne house.
explanation.definitionFit: The 1939 Civil War epic starring Vivien Leigh shares its year with The Wizard of Oz, whose house was blown away.

clue.text: Nuts off the menu for Rover?

parts.note: a dish off the menu is a no
nuts means crazy

explanation.surface: A dog called Rover denied nuts at dinner.
explanation.walkthrough: Rover looks like a dog's name but means a wanderer.
explanation.definitionFit: A rover is a person who wanders from place to place, which is what a nomad does.

clue.text: Part of football pitch where energy's located?

parts.words: Part of football pitch where energy's located
parts.note: surface reading: the area of the pitch where players expend most effort
setter's reading: E for energy is the letter in the middle of the word field

explanation.surface: A coach describes where the work gets done on the pitch.
explanation.walkthrough: E stands for energy, and E is the central letter of FIELD.
explanation.definitionFit: The midfield is the central area of a football pitch between the two penalty areas.

clue.text: Rusty old, old nails very, very strong, marines concluding

indicators.note: to nail is to pin down, so the pair holds the next piece between them
concluding puts the last piece at the end

parts.note: O for old again
RM is the Royal Marines
fff, fortississimo, is the musical marking for extremely loud
O is a common abbreviation for old

explanation.surface: An old iron bar, very tough, finished by the marines.
explanation.walkthrough: Rusty looks like corroded metal but means out of practice; musical dynamics stack the letter f, so one more f means louder.
explanation.definitionFit: Rusty means out of practice, so a player who is rusty is performing below their usual standard.

clue.text: Farm egg I tend to put out in kitchen drawer?

indicators.note: putting out the items lays them in a fresh order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A farmer setting out eggs in a kitchen drawer.
explanation.walkthrough: A drawer looks like the sliding box in a cupboard, but here it is something that draws, or attracts.
explanation.definitionFit: A fridge magnet is found in a kitchen and attracts metal, so it is jokingly a kitchen drawer.

clue.text: See 23
Fibre ultimately absent, lady keen to knit without threads

indicators.note: knitting works strands into a new pattern, so the letters are rearranged
absent means the letter is missing from the other words
ultimately means at the end, so the final letter is wanted

parts.note: last letter of fibre
taken as written

explanation.surface: An eager knitter runs out of yarn.
explanation.walkthrough: One E is removed from LADY KEEN before rearranging.
explanation.definitionFit: Threads is slang for clothes, so being without threads means being unclothed.

clue.text: Cut costs, bound to save money, initially

indicators.note: to save something is to keep it, so one word holds the letter

parts.note: skip means to leap or bound

indicators.note: initially means only the first letter is used

parts.note: first letter of money

explanation.surface: Economising advice: you are obliged to put money aside.
explanation.walkthrough: Bound reads as obliged but is the verb meaning jump.
explanation.definitionFit: To skimp is to spend less than needed, economising on something, which cuts costs.

clue.text: See 28
What dog might wish to do to be lifted?

definitions.text: What dog might wish to do
definitions.meaning: first meaning: walkies is the British word for taking a dog out for a walk
second meaning: in British slang, a thing that goes walkies goes missing, usually stolen

explanation.surface: A dog hoping to be picked up and carried.
explanation.walkthrough: Lifted looks like raised off the ground but is slang for stolen.
explanation.definitionFit: Go walkies is British slang for disappearing or being stolen, as well as a dog's outing.

clue.text: Noughts: zero no good as a particular number

parts.note: a score of zero in tennis
O looks like a zero
NG is short for no good

explanation.surface: A maths puzzle: rows of zeros that add up to a specific figure.
explanation.walkthrough: Number looks like a figure, but it means a piece of music.
explanation.definitionFit: A number is a song or musical piece, and a love song is one particular kind of it.

clue.text: Animal impression

definitions.meaning: second meaning: a mark stamped into wax

explanation.walkthrough: Impression looks like an imitation of an animal, but it is a stamped mark.
explanation.definitionFit: A seal is a flippered sea mammal, and also the design pressed into wax to authenticate a document.

clue.text: Careless line failing to impress good man

indicators.note: impressing something presses it into a surface, putting one letter inside
a failing thing is breaking down, so these letters fall into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
G is short for good
a gentleman

explanation.surface: A sloppy chat-up line that fails to win over a decent man.
explanation.walkthrough: Impress reads as dazzle, but it means press G into the mixed-up LINE.
explanation.definitionFit: Negligent means failing to take proper care, a direct synonym of careless.

clue.text: One, two, three and four back in house

indicators.note: back means the letters are read in the opposite direction

parts.note: every number up to four is all of IV, the Roman four

explanation.surface: Counting to four inside a house.
explanation.definitionFit: A villa is a large country or holiday house, so it is one kind of house.
